# pedplot

**pedplot** offers a fresh take on pedigree plotting in R. It produces plots similar to **kinship2** and early versions of **pedtools**, but with better alignments in many complex pedigrees and several novel features. In particular,
**pedplot** is designed for use by other packages, simplifying downstream manipulation of plot elements. It was developed for the [pedsuite](https://pedsuite.org/), but also works with ordinary data frame input.

## Installation

**pedplot** is not on CRAN yet, but can be installed from GitHub:
```{r, eval=FALSE}
pak::pak("magnusdv/pedplot")
```

## Examples

The following examples illustrate some of the features of **pedplot**. For convenience we use **pedtools** to create the pedigrees. 
```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(pedtools)
library(pedplot)
```

#### Fewer duplications
Complex pedigrees sometimes require duplicating individuals in the plot. As such duplications tend to clutter the display, **pedplot** tries hard to use as few as possible. The following example shows a half-sib mating circle. Here **pedplot** needs only one repeated person, while **pedtools** 2.12.0 uses four duplications.

```{r fewer-copies, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.3, message=F, echo = -1}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
x = halfSibPed() |> addSon(3) |> addSon(c(1, 6))
plot(x, title = "pedtools 2.12.0")
plotPed(x, title = "pedplot")
```

#### Hidden founders 
A novel feature of **pedplot** is the ability to hide selected founders. This often simplify the display of large pedigrees.

```{r hidden-founders, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.3, echo = -1}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
x = linearPed(2)
plotPed(x, title = "Full pedigree")
plotPed(x, hideFounders = c(2, 4), title = "Founders hidden")
```

#### Exact sizes 
Symbol sizes, padding (inner margin) and outer margins can be specified exactly, in mm, cm or inches. Padding can also be specified in "symbol sizes" (the width of a person symbol). Here are two examples:

```{r exact-size, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.2, echo = -1}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plotPed(nuclearPed(), 
        symbolsize = 1, symbolsizeUnit = "cm",
        margins = 2, marginsUnit = "cm")
box("plot", lty = 3); box("figure", col = "blue")

plotPed(nuclearPed(),  # auto symbol size
        padding = 1, paddingUnit = "sym",
        margins = 3, marginsUnit = "mm")
box("plot", lty = 3); box("figure", col = "blue")
```

#### Colours and annotations
Borders, fills and hatch lines can be controlled independently and separately for each person.

```{r colours, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=3, out.width="55%"}
plotPed(singleton(1), cex = 4, lwd = 10, 
        hatched = 1, hatchDensity = 5, hatchLwd = 3,
        col = "blue", fill = "green", hatchCol = "red")
```

#### Multiple pedigrees 
A list of pedigrees can be plotted in one figure.

```{r multiple, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
peds = list(nuclearPed(), singleton(), cousinPed())
plotPed(peds)
```

See `?plotPed` for more options. For finer control, `alignPed()`, `scalePed()`,
`partsPed()` and `drawPed()` give access to the individual plotting steps.
